HG12-p3c.was_md: A hypnotist working on me can't interact with my subconscious mind quickly enough to get the detailed feedback needed to know what's going on in my mind, since they aren't IN my mind. (Of course, there are advantages to having a skilled guide, since they may be able to see things I'm blind to, and can help me keep the process regulated and safe.) But doing it myself has one advantage nobody outside can copy: immediate dialogue with my own system.

HG12-p7e.was_md: Some benefits arrived the next morning or a few days later. After one loveyhuasca self-hypnosis session, I woke in what felt like an answer to prayer. I’d been dealing with a lot of lust energy and worrying it could pull me into a relationship that wasn’t right. I asked the subconscious to connect the heart chakra with the sacral chakra—to bring the love energy and sex energy into the same current. The next morning I woke in a kind of “perfected” love state. I didn’t feel that I needed to find a woman; the divine feminine felt somehow at zero distance from my heart. Ordinary interaction dissolved the state, but for a while it showed me a possibility my mind and heart may permit when the desire is sincere.

HG15-p9e.was_md: What is the difference between a human doer and a human being? If you don’t feel good enough as a human being, you will try to become good enough as a human doer by for example being beautiful, doing something well, being smart, having a certain status, being spiritual, etc. Those can all be real gifts. They become a bargain for belonging when failing in these areas feels like losing yourself.
HG15-p9e.new_md: What is the difference between a human doer and a human being? If you don’t feel good enough as a human being, you will try to become good enough as a human doer by for example being beautiful, doing something well, being smart, having a certain status, being spiritual, etc. Those can all be real gifts, but if failing at one of them feels like losing yourself, it has become a way to buy belonging.

HG15-p11t.was_md: Give your inner child the opportunity to do something that has no value on its own and that it doesn’t need to be good at for its resume. For example painting, dancing, gardening, learning a language, playing a sport, doing volunteer work, playing a musical instrument, etc. Because often your inner parent tells your inner child that it is supposed to be good at something as soon as it starts doing it. And that’s not good because your inner child will get humiliated that it isn’t good at it. The adult in you can answer, “We’re finding out whether we enjoy this, not proving our worth.” So try things out long enough until the humiliation is gone.
